races.name: Here Come The Girls EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Cousin Rachel
runners_data.note: Showed fair form finishing eighth on Good ground over 6f on debut, but Tim Eaves and Kevin Ryan's filly is a genuine hold-up horse whose natural rearward position is compromised in a five-runner field — she needs pace to run at and the race may not provide it.

runners_data.name: Lady Caroline Lamb
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston sends out this lightly raced filly third time out on a longer 7f trip over good ground for Carlisle; her unknown style (U) is the key uncertainty and she could be placed anywhere tactically, making her the wildcard of the race.

runners_data.name: Fern Clyde
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's filly is the clear pace anchor here, improving steadily through a form string of 6-4-3-1, with her sole win coming on Good ground over 6f; the step up to 7½f is the only query, but her hood and David Allan's positive riding style suggest she will be sent for home early.

runners_data.name: Little Lady Karen
runners_data.note: Karl Burke's filly ran a respectable third on Good ground over 6f last time, 19 days ago, and the hold-up style she naturally adopts means she will need to find late cover — over 7½f she may get a stronger test that plays to her staying profile, but she is dependent on a fast pace.

runners_data.name: Rogue Passion
runners_data.note: Ed Bethell's filly was beaten fourth over 7f on Soft last time for Tudhope, and the switch to Good to Firm ground is a potential positive for her; she is another natural holder who will sit and wait, meaning she too relies on Fern Clyde setting a brisk enough clip to bring her back into the finish.

races.paceDynamic: Fern Clyde is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no serious pace rival to challenge her, she should stride into a comfortable lead from the outset and dictate on Good to Firm ground over 7½f at Beverley. The three hold-up types — Cousin Rachel, Little Lady Karen, and Rogue Passion — will be chasing from off the pace, while Lady Caroline Lamb's unknown style leaves her tactical position uncertain heading into this novice heat. With Fern Clyde able to set her own tempo unchallenged, this race shape strongly favours prominent and front-running profiles that can control the gallop and avoid the traffic risks that closers will face against a potentially uncontested leader. The field contains more hold-up types than can realistically benefit from a late run in a race where the pace may not be strong enough to bring them back into contention.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fern Clyde Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Fern Clyde goes forward immediately and settles into a comfortable solo lead through the early stages.
scenarios.body: If Fern Clyde goes forward immediately and settles into a comfortable solo lead through the early stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Fern Clyde sets a genuinely strong pace that burns her out and the closers find clear daylight in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Fern Clyde sets a genuinely strong pace that burns her out and the closers find clear daylight in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lady Caroline Lamb Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Caroline Lamb's unknown style proves to be naturally prominent and she tracks Fern Clyde before asserting her class.
scenarios.body: If Lady Caroline Lamb's unknown style proves to be naturally prominent and she tracks Fern Clyde before asserting her class.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Cousin Rachel Lands Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Cousin Rachel overcomes her redistributed midfield position and finds a clear, unimpeded run to deliver her hold-up challenge.
scenarios.body: If Cousin Rachel overcomes her redistributed midfield position and finds a clear, unimpeded run to deliver her hold-up challenge.

watchPoints.text: Fern Clyde's stamina over 7½f is the pivotal question — if she ties up in the final furlong having led throughout, the entire race shape inverts and the hold-up horses flood past her.
Cousin Rachel is tagged as racing out of role in a five-runner field; watch whether T Eaves elects to push her forward against her natural style, which would significantly change the pace dynamic.

Lady Caroline Lamb's unknown style means Connor Beasley could adopt any position — if he tracks Fern Clyde prominently from the outset, she becomes an immediate competitive danger rather than an afterthought.

With three hold-up types (Cousin Rachel, Little Lady Karen, Rogue Passion) all needing a pace to run at, monitor the early fractions — if Fern Clyde cruises at a steady gallop, the closers may simply never get competitive.

Good to Firm conditions are confirmed for this race despite the card header showing Good — the faster surface will suit Fern Clyde's front-running style and may expose any hold-up horses who struggled on Soft last time, particularly Rogue Passion.

races.name: Beverley Racecourse Supporting Racing Staff Week Handicap

runners_data.name: Tattie Bogle
runners_data.note: Jason Hart's mount has won at 7f on Good ground and posted a string of placed efforts in similar conditions; as a genuine hold-up type she is ideally suited to a race where one front-runner controls the pace and a clear run develops late, though connections will need this shape to deliver a clean passage.

runners_data.name: This Farh
runners_data.note: Won at 8f on Good ground last time and carries headgear (p — probably a hood or similar); Rowan Scott is an economical jockey who will keep this hold-up horse covered up in rear and produce a sustained challenge, with three wins in fifteen similar-going runs showing the profile is reliable in these conditions.

runners_data.name: Roaring Ralph
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has won five of his last six, all front-running at 7-8f on Good and Standard; Rhys Elliott rides and the STYLE_FIT tag notes he is operating out of role as the map's sole front-runner rather than a pressing horse — his dominance here is circumstantial but real, and he simply has no rival willing to force him off the front.

runners_data.name: Coolree
runners_data.note: Trainer S England sends this seven-year-old in fair form — two wins from recent 8f Good starts — and he wears a tp (tongue strap and/or pad); he is a natural prominent type who will look to press Roaring Ralph and could exploit any weakness if the pace lifts, though his best form has come at 8f rather than this sharper 7½f.

runners_data.name: Midsummer Storm
runners_data.note: K R Burke's three-year-old has the fewest runs of any in the field (just three), returning after 45 days off, and sits with a genuinely unknown style (U); without a confirmed tactical shape, S H James will have to make a decision on the fly, and while the Burke yard fires horses back in good order the lack of prominent or hold-up form runs against a definitive style read.

runners_data.name: Sunny Orange
runners_data.note: T D Easterby's six-year-old has strong front-running tendencies and wears a hood (p), but with Roaring Ralph and Coolree both ahead of him for early position he is likely to find himself racing wider and further back than he would like — his ten runs in similar going show wins are possible but his handicap mark of OR 60 and STYLE_FIT discount make this a tough ask from a compromised position.

runners_data.name: Evocative Spark
runners_data.note: Wears a visor (v), which often sharpens focus, and John Riches has a live 1/2 trainer-14-day strike rate; three wins from seven-furlong Good ground races in his last five starts give him strong profile credentials, and as a prominent type at the lower end of this competitive bunch he could be dangerous if he settles just behind the front pair and pounces.

races.paceDynamic: Roaring Ralph is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Coolree and Evocative Spark as genuine prominent-type rivals in a seven-runner field, he should be able to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Beverley. Coolree and Evocative Spark will press for early position but neither is likely to force a truly punishing pace, meaning Roaring Ralph can bowl along at his own rhythm and preserve energy for the finish. Sunny Orange is a natural prominent racer who has been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more front-running and pressing types than can all secure their preferred spots — Roaring Ralph and Coolree are best placed to actually hold those positions, leaving Sunny Orange racing further back than ideal. This shape — a steady, controlled pace set by one dominant front-runner — strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce a sustained late run into a clean closing stretch, putting Tattie Bogle and This Farh in the most advantageous tactical position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Roaring Ralph Controls, Closers Sweep
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Ralph leads at a controlled tempo and the pace stays honest but not scorching, hold-up horses get a clean run to the line.
scenarios.body: If Roaring Ralph leads at a controlled tempo and the pace stays honest but not scorching, hold-up horses get a clean run to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Roaring Ralph Leads, Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Roaring Ralph gets a completely uncontested lead and turns the race into a solo time trial, allowing him to dictate every yard and quicken away from rivals.
scenarios.body: If Roaring Ralph gets a completely uncontested lead and turns the race into a solo time trial, allowing him to dictate every yard and quicken away from rivals.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Press Hard, Messy Shape
scenarios.trigger: If Coolree and Evocative Spark both push up aggressively early and force a stronger-than-expected pace on Roaring Ralph.
scenarios.body: If Coolree and Evocative Spark both push up aggressively early and force a stronger-than-expected pace on Roaring Ralph.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rain Or Incident Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpected early incident, slow start, or significant going change alters the predicted race flow entirely.
scenarios.body: If an unexpected early incident, slow start, or significant going change alters the predicted race flow entirely.

watchPoints.text: Tattie Bogle and This Farh — if Roaring Ralph is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and the pace is merely honest, both hold-up horses are poised to produce the strongest closing runs in the field; their finishing kick on Good to Firm ground is the single biggest danger to any front-runner.

Roaring Ralph — if Coolree or Evocative Spark decides to push the pace aggressively in the first half mile, Roaring Ralph's unbeaten front-running sequence could be tested for the first time; watch how settled Rhys Elliott allows him to travel.

Sunny Orange — drawn in a field with more prominent types than can all hold their position, he risks being buffeted early or racing wide; if he fails to find a rhythm in an unnatural position his chance diminishes sharply despite his OR 60 making him the lowest-rated runner.

Midsummer Storm — the 45-day absence and unknown tactical style mean K R Burke's three-year-old is a wildcard; if the yard has her tuned up and S H James decides to sit midfield and produce a late run, a fresh horse can occasionally outpace more exposed rivals at this trip.

Evocative Spark's visor — this is headgear worth monitoring at the stalls: a sharp-jumping visored horse in a small seven-runner field can grab an uncontested position behind the leader and make the race difficult for closers if the pace remains controlled.

races.name: Big Racing Weekender Next 3 And 4 July Restricted Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Beverley Annual Badgeholders Handicap

runners_data.name: Bruce Banner
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse who drops to 1m4f after running with credit over 1m2f and 2m; Jason Hart rides and the visor is applied, but two placed efforts from four runs on similar going suggest consistency without a winning move — 5-day turnaround keeps him fresh.|

runners_data.name: Lednikov
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type whose sole win from 15 similar-going runs underlines the class ceiling; Elle-May Croot takes over and the blinkers are fitted, though five-from-twelve at 1m2f then 1m4f on good surfaces shows he tries the trip without converting — 10-day break is fine.|

runners_data.name: Jedhi Knight
runners_data.note: The OR-51 four-year-old showed a 1-4-2-3 sequence before a reappearance fifth; D Nolan is in the saddle and though the blinkers are on, his soft-ground form in bumpers and staying trips contrasts with today's faster surface — he is a hold-up horse shunted to midfield here because the map is saturated with rear-runners, tempering his position-based chance.|

runners_data.name: Dandy's Angel
runners_data.note: Wainwright's nine-year-old has 1W-2P from 15 runs on similar going and showed form at 1m and 1m2f in good-ground conditions; her recent third at 1m2f Good is the best current-form angle in the race, though she is a hold-up horse depicted in midfield by necessity rather than preference, and Tom Kiely-Marshall will need to make a tactical decision early.|

runners_data.name: Princess Vivi
runners_data.note: The four-year-old filly has headgear (p) applied and ran second over 1m on good ground — the step to 1m4f today is new territory and her Flat form has been at 7f-1m; Cam Hardie takes the ride, and while she is a hold-up type placed at midfield on the map due to a crowded rear, the stamina question at this trip is the primary issue.|

runners_data.name: Arch Legend
runners_data.note: Carr's five-year-old has a poor record over today's distances on comparable surfaces — 0W-1P from six similar-going runs and a form string of 8587-0 paints a difficult picture; J P Sullivan partners her and she is a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield purely by the field's composition, limiting the value of that positioning.|

runners_data.name: Satyress
runners_data.note: Bethell has only two runners in the last fortnight but this four-year-old ran a fair fourth on good going over 1m2f last time; S D Bowen comes in and the horse's honest form at 1m-1m2f makes the step to 1m4f the key query — a hold-up horse in practice, she sits mid-map here by necessity and is the one whose recent form is marginally the freshest in a difficult race.|

runners_data.name: Sweet Cicely
runners_data.note: Sowersby's four-year-old has finished ninth, tenth, eleventh, tenth, and ninth in her last five outings on good and similar surfaces — this is an extremely low-grade form profile and the headgear (p) has not changed the pattern; William Pyle takes the ride and she is placed at midfield on the map by redistribution alone, with nothing in her recent performances to suggest a threat.|

races.paceDynamic: This 1m4f Beverley handicap is an extreme hold-up dominated field with no confirmed front-runner among the eight runners, meaning the early gallop is likely to be tentative and the race compressed into a sprint finish up Beverley's stiff closing furlong. With every runner in the field carrying a hold-up profile, the pace scenario defaults to a slow, dawdling early tempo before a bunch kick in the straight — a shape that paradoxically suits whichever horse can position closest to the pace from the off without burning energy. The field holds considerably more genuine hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear; Jedhi Knight, Dandy's Angel, Princess Vivi, Arch Legend, Satyress, and Sweet Cicely are all true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield slots they are unlikely to naturally inhabit, with Bruce Banner and Lednikov the marginally most confirmed hold-up profiles toward the back. The tactical verdict is unambiguous: this race favours a horse who can break well, position in the first half of the field from a slow pace, and produce a sustained gallop in the final two furlongs — horses with stamina, a decent recent run, and a jockey willing to make an early move will have a decisive edge over true sit-and-wait horses caught flat-footed in a sprint.

scenarios.body: If the race drifts through the early stages at a crawl and the sprint kicks in from the home turn, rewarding those with proven 1m4f stamina and a forward position.

scenarios.label: D

scenarios.body: If an unusually fast early pace is set and the front group ties themselves up, allowing genuine hold-up horses to reel them in from off the pace in the final furlong.

watchPoints.text: No confirmed front-runner in a field of eight means the early gallop is in nobody's hands — watch the start closely for which jockey blinks first and pushes forward, as whoever establishes even a modest lead in the first three furlongs has a structural advantage on this track.

Dandy's Angel and Princess Vivi are both genuine hold-up horses whose jockeys may feel compelled to push forward from the gates given the leadership vacuum — if either ends up on the pace from choice rather than necessity, their stamina at 1m4f becomes an immediate question.

Satyress drops significantly in distance profile (best form at 1m-1m2f) stepping to 1m4f — if the early pace is genuinely slow and the race becomes a sprint, her quicker finishing style could flatter her, but watch whether S D Bowen commits her early or waits too long in a cavalry charge.

Beverley's uphill finish at 1m4f punishes horses who are flat-footed or wide in the straight — with a field of eight hold-up horses, draw and early position off a slow tempo could be as decisive as outright ability, making the first furlong unusually important to monitor.

Bruce Banner's five-day turnaround after running fifth over 1m2f is the shortest gap in the field and worth monitoring in the pre-race market — if Jason Hart is instructed to make more use of him than the hold-up profile suggests, the form angle over this trip on good ground gives him a legitimate place chance.

races.name: Humberside Airport Handicap

runners_data.name: Percy's Daydream
runners_data.note: D O'Meara yard in solid 10/60 form over 14 days and David Tudhope in the saddle — this horse has won over 10f on Good and has a course record of three wins and seven places from eleven similar-ground starts, making it perfectly placed to exploit sole front-running control here, though the style-fit tag is a reminder it may not always secure that berth.

runners_data.name: Mao Shang Wong
runners_data.note: Same O'Meara yard as Percy's Daydream, which is worth noting for market purposes — won over 10f on Good ground and has form figures of 1/10f/GOO in its recent history, making it the most credible hold-up threat, though its stable companion is likely to be well ahead of it at halfway.

runners_data.name: Helmsley
runners_data.note: Trainer I Furtado sends this horse out 10 days fresh with a headgear flag — in truth a genuine hold-up type whose two runs this year on soft and good have yielded a second and a sixth, and while it appears on the map in midfield due to redistribution, it will race from the rear and needs a collapse in front to get involved.

runners_data.name: Qitaal
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old for C Johnston, who has a 4/34 recent strike rate, returning just five days after its last run — the strongest similar-going profile in the race with eight runs on Good ground including two placed efforts, and at OR 75 the ratings compress, but a natural hold-up style means it requires something to come to it rather than making its own luck.

runners_data.name: Titian
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old wearing a hood for Miss J A Camacho, whose yard is 4/20 over 14 days — a confirmed hold-up horse placed to midfield on the map by redistribution, and with recent form showing 16th, 6th, 6th, 11th, and 11th in its last five, the style-fit concern and age make this the longest shot to deliver in any scenario.

races.paceDynamic: Percy's Daydream is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger likely to dispute the lead, will control the tempo from the front across this 1m2f trip on Good to Firm ground at Beverley. The pace is likely to be measured and sustainable rather than scorching — a lone leader setting an honest but uncontested gallop means the race will be run at Percy's Daydream's own rhythm, with the hold-up horses Mao Shang Wong, Qitaal, Helmsley, and Titian all forced to track from the rear or midfield. Helmsley and Titian are true hold-up horses that have been redistributed to show midfield on the map simply because the field is dominated by closers — they are unlikely to get any position closer to the pace than their natural style dictates. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile — a controlled leader on fast ground at a track that suits those who travel well through a race, with no one to force a genuinely searching gallop and the closers needing something to go wrong in front to get involved.

scenarios.title: Leader Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Daydream dictates an uncontested, measured pace and the closers are given too much to do.
scenarios.body: If Percy's Daydream dictates an uncontested, measured pace and the closers are given too much to do.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Daydream's lead proves unsustainable or the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late flourish.
scenarios.body: If Percy's Daydream's lead proves unsustainable or the pace is genuinely strong enough to set up a late flourish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Type Picks Through

scenarios.body: If the early pace is truly pedestrian and bunching allows a hold-up horse to creep closer than expected through the race.

scenarios.label: D

scenarios.trigger: If market leaders underperform and the redistributed horses race more prominently than their tags suggest.
scenarios.body: If market leaders underperform and the redistributed horses race more prominently than their tags suggest.

watchPoints.text: Percy's Daydream — watch whether Tudhope is allowed to stride clear unchallenged from the gate; if no one follows it up, this race is effectively run to order for a front-runner.

Mao Shang Wong — the O'Meara yard double entry is worth tracking in the market; if this horse is sent off shorter than expected, connections may have a preferred runner and Percy's Daydream could be ridden to assist.

Qitaal — five days since last run is tight, and Connor Beasley will need to position aggressively for a hold-up horse on a track where fast ground can make late charges difficult; watch its early placement.

Helmsley — the headgear change is the key flag here; if it produces an early forward move it was not showing before, the redistribution note becomes relevant, but recent form offers little evidence it will do so.

Going drift — the official going is Good to Firm for this race specifically; any significant market moves late could reflect inside knowledge of how the track is riding by the time this race goes off, which would particularly affect the hold-up horses' chances.

races.name: Racing TV Extra On racingtv.com Handicap

runners_data.name: Ice Show
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for D O'Meara with D Tudhope in the saddle — a powerful booking — who steps up to 1m2f on Good To Firm after run-style-consistent efforts at shorter; no wins yet but each-way profile suits a sprint-finish scenario.

runners_data.name: Sahm Naif
runners_data.note: James Horton runner handled by Jason Hart who has run four times and shown flashes of ability on Good ground; 1m2f is a step up in trip and, with no pace in this race, may find himself pushed further forward than ideal but could use that position to advantage.

runners_data.name: Wadacre Geisha
runners_data.note: C Johnston filly with Connor Beasley who holds a placed run on Good ground and shaped with promise over 1m2f — her true running style is off the pace, but the cramped hold-up market here means she is unlikely to get as far back as she needs; STYLE_FIT tempers confidence.

runners_data.name: King Of Yorkshire
runners_data.note: Jedd O'Keeffe gelding back after 47 days off — the freshness angle is worth noting — but form figures of 875-0 on varied ground are uninspiring, and racing off the pace in a race that may not produce a true end-to-end test makes his task harder; STYLE_FIT applies.

runners_data.name: Turton
runners_data.note: J Tate's three-year-old carries a finish-fade flag which is a serious concern in a race virtually guaranteed to end in a sprint; the blinkers are noted but his last three runs show a pattern of weakening, and being displaced from his natural trailing position makes things harder still.

runners_data.name: Resdev Time
runners_data.note: M & D Easterby handler with Joanna Mason up, this filly has finished fifth or worse in nine recent starts on similar ground — consistent without threatening — and her hold-up style will again be compromised by the crowded rear-field dynamics here; STYLE_FIT consideration applies.

runners_data.name: Royal Sizzler
runners_data.note: M Dods runner equipped with a hood and carrying a finish-fade flag — a double concern in a compressed sprint scenario — has run 11th, 10th and 5th in recent starts and is 36 days fresh; going is fine but structural profile makes it hard to see how she wins from any position.

runners_data.name: Eva The Deeva
runners_data.note: N Tinkler's filly ridden by Faye McManoman who has posted a 7th on Good and shaped with some promise; the 26-day gap is fine, the Good To Firm surface is consistent with her history, and at the bottom of the weights (125lbs) she gets every pound of assistance the handicapper can offer.

races.paceDynamic: This 1m2f Beverley handicap is a genuinely pace-starved race — every runner in the field of eight carries a hold-up style tag, meaning no confirmed front-runner exists to set a true gallop from the outset. With the going confirmed Good To Firm throughout the card, the likely outcome is a dawdling early pace as runners jockey for position before a sharp, compressed sprint develops in the home straight, favouring those who travel economically and can sustain a late effort over this trip. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Ice Show, Sahm Naif, Wadacre Geisha, King Of Yorkshire, Turton, Resdev Time, Royal Sizzler and Eva The Deeva are all natural off-the-pace horses, meaning several will inevitably end up racing further forward than they would prefer, and those with any degree of speed to press on early — such as Sahm Naif and Ice Show — may find themselves prominent by default. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours those with a turn of foot to exploit a falsely-run, sprint-finish scenario, and horses who stay on steadily or fade in the closing stages — Turton and Royal Sizzler both carry finish-fade flags — are at a structural disadvantage.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Sahm Naif or Ice Show drift forward to fill the pace vacuum in the opening furlong — whoever secures an uncontested lead on Good To Firm ground at Beverley will be very difficult to dislodge.

Turton and Royal Sizzler both carry finish-fade flags in a race almost certain to end in a sprint; if either gets outpaced at the critical moment, they are unlikely to find more and could drop away quickly.

Wadacre Geisha and King Of Yorkshire are true hold-up horses displaced toward midfield — watch whether they can find racing room in the home straight given the entire field will be converging from a similar position.

Eva The Deeva carries the lowest weight in the field at 125lbs — in a compressed sprint finish on fast ground where margins are narrow, that allowance could prove meaningful if she travels smoothly into the straight.

The going has been confirmed Good To Firm all afternoon at Beverley despite the nominal Good description — horses with proven form on fast ground or a Good To Firm sim-going record hold a small but genuine edge over those without it.

races.name: Go Racing In Yorkshire Future Stars Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Oasis Cover
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the race and holds a dominant positional advantage; three days since last run keeps her fresh, Beverley 5f suits an on-pace style on Good to Firm, and E Bethell's stable is 4/24 in the 14-day window — her chance hinges entirely on whether she translates her lead position into winning control rather than simply front-running and fading.

runners_data.name: Jack Rabbit Slims
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 5f on Good ground including a runner-up finish, giving him the best recent form evidence of the hold-up brigade; tp headgear sharpens focus, Jack Nicholls takes the ride, and a trainer with 0/6 in the 14-day window tempers expectations despite the course-distance profile suiting.

runners_data.name: Dabbling
runners_data.note: Five runs without a win or place in this grade, and a record of 0W0P on similar going paints a modest picture; Tom Kiely-Marshall is booked but the 19-day absence and a form string that reads 59-675 offers little encouragement for a horse that needs things to fall perfectly from a rear position.

runners_data.name: Brain Freeze
runners_data.note: Won over 5f on Good ground and has placed three times in similar conditions — statistically the strongest hold-up horse on going evidence; blinkered and has genuine pace claims, but the redistribution note reflects that he will not get the relaxed rear position his style demands and his STYLE_FIT score of 0.91 should temper confidence accordingly.

runners_data.name: Power Of Chora
runners_data.note: Six runs without a win, 0W0P on similar going, and a form string of 7-8668 tells a consistent story of mid-division finishing; tp headgear is retained but Joey Ramsden's stable is quiet (1/11 over 14 days) and his natural hold-up style will be squeezed in a field of similarly-minded rivals.

runners_data.name: Sparkling Wine
runners_data.note: Showed a 2nd-place finish over 5f on Soft, suggesting she handles testing ground, though her Good-ground record reads 0W0P from three runs; the M Dods yard is active (4/26 in 14 days) and the light weight of 121lbs is a minor plus, but she is a genuine hold-up type who will be shuffled forward into an awkward mid-race position.

runners_data.name: Tanaka
runners_data.note: Headgear (hood) and a trainer firing in form (D O'Meara 6/55 over 14 days) are the main positives; 0W0P on Good ground from four attempts and a form string of 640-75 offers little to build a case on, and like several rivals here he will find his natural hold-up role compromised by the overcrowding at the rear of this field.

races.paceDynamic: Oasis Cover is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 7-runner 5f Beverley sprint and, with no genuine rival to challenge for the lead, she will dictate an uncontested, sustainable gallop from the outset on Good to Firm ground. Behind her, the field is almost entirely composed of hold-up horses — Brain Freeze, Power Of Chora, Sparkling Wine, Tanaka, Jack Rabbit Slims and Dabbling all carry hold-up profiles, yet the map cannot accommodate them all at the rear; several will be pushed into positions closer to the pace than their natural style demands. With a single pace-setter controlling fractions and no pressure from behind, this is a classic scenario for a lone leader to find a rhythm, conserve energy and prove very difficult to reel in over a short 5f trip. The race shape strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile — Oasis Cover sets the tone and any horse that can travel close to the pace without being a true hold-up type gains a meaningful tactical advantage; deep closers face the hardest task of all.

scenarios.title: Oasis Cover Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Oasis Cover breaks cleanly and is allowed to dictate an uncontested, measured gallop with no rival willing or able to press her.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If two or more of the redistributed horses break sharply and force Oasis Cover into a contested gallop that she cannot sustain.

scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Chaotically

watchPoints.text: Oasis Cover — watch for a clean break from the stalls; if she is slow away and surrenders the lead to any of the hold-up types forced forward, her entire scenario collapses and the race shape becomes genuinely unpredictable.

Brain Freeze — despite being redistributed to midfield on the map, he has the strongest hold-up Going record in the field (1W3P on similar ground) and if apprentice Rhys Elliott conjures a clear passage from two out he is the most dangerous individual closer.

Jack Rabbit Slims — his two placed efforts over 5f on Good ground make him the most credible threat from off the pace; watch whether tp headgear keeps him focused enough to land a challenge if Oasis Cover's lead begins to shorten in the final furlong.

Sparkling Wine and Tanaka — both carry the lightest weights (121lbs) and are trained by in-form stables; neither has won on Good ground but their low burdens could manufacture a surprise if the pace scenario unravels into a late sprint finish.
